answer: PoA resists Sybil attacks by binding each identity to bonded collateral and linking equivocation evidence across identities. If k coordinated identities sign conflicting statements, the protocol charges correlated penalties of O(k^2); detecting a managed swarm also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss through asymmetric depreciation, accelerating a downward spiral. Thus, an attacker cannot cheaply expand an atlas of agents, since even copper-sized stakes become economically prohibitive.
